quote: Wherefore my counsel is, that we hold fast ever to the heavenly way and follow after justice and virtue always, considering that the soul is immortal and able to endure every sort of good and every sort of evil. Thus shall we live dear to one another and to the gods, both while remaining here and when, like conquerors in the games who go round to gather gifts, we receive our reward. And it shall be well with us both in this life and in the pilgrimage of a thousand years which we have been describing.
source: Plato, The Republic, Book X, 621c to d, the closing lines (Socrates) (trans. Benjamin Jowett, 1888)
speaker: Socrates
note: The translator year was corrected from 1871 to 1888. This wording, comma after counsel is included, is Jowett’s third edition, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1888, read in a scan of that edition. The 1871 first edition was not seen, and a second Gutenberg setting prints the sentence without that comma, so the card names the edition whose page was read.

evidence.where: The Clarendon Press third edition of 1888, the title page reading THE THIRD EDITION REVISED AND CORRECTED THROUGHOUT and the imprint M DCCC LXXXVIII, read in the archive.org OCR scan, where the three sentences close the dialogue immediately before the index; Project Gutenberg ebook 1497 prints the same wording, while Gutenberg ebook 150 is a different setting that drops the comma after counsel is
evidence.edition: The Republic of Plato, translated into English by B. Jowett, third edition, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1888
evidence.locator: Book X, 621c to d, the last three sentences of the dialogue, Socrates to Glaucon at the end of the myth of Er

reason: The three sentences are exact in the 1888 third edition, which is the only Jowett printing I actually opened, and they are the closing lines of the work, so the fame test holds. The proposal claimed 1871, which I could not check and which may well differ, since two Gutenberg settings of Jowett already differ over one comma. Socrates is the speaker and is named. Not shipped, not banned, Plato is new to the year.
